item.title: Incarico di ricerca: GIUR-09/A INTERNATIONAL LAW (Univ. Catt. S.Cuore)
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-12-15 16:00
Institution: Univ. Catt. S.Cuore, Milano
Field: Law / 12/GIUR-09 Diritto internazionale

The selected candidate will conduct research in the field of Public International Law, with particular reference to the interactions between international law, regional legal frameworks, and domestic legal systems in the regulation of emerging technologies and their implications for the protection of human rights, with a particular focus on energy justice. The research activity will involve the analysis and monitoring of legal, institutional, and policy developments concerning artificial intelligence at the international, regional, and national levels, as well as the examination of how customary and treaty-based international law shape the governance of emerging technologies.

item.description:
Deadline: 2026-12-11 13:00
Institution: Univ. TORINO, Turin
Field: Law / 12/GIUR-16 Storia del diritto medievale e moderno

To this end, the research will involve the following activities: 1. The examination of the primary sources and the archival and bibliographical materials relevant to the research; 2. item.title: Incarico di ricerca: The DNSH Principle and the Transformation of Public Procurement: Administrative Discretion, Environmental Sustainability and the Evolving Responsibilities of Contracting Authorities (Univ. TORINO)
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-12-11 13:00
Institution: Univ. TORINO, Turin
Field: Law / 12/GIUR-06 Diritto amministrativo e pubblico

The research will examine the role of the Do No Significant Harm (DNSH) principle in the evolution of EU environmental law and sustainable public procurement. It will investigate the principle’s legal nature, its relationship with sustainable development, environmental integration and EU policy coherence, and its implications for administrative discretion and the responsibilities of contracting authorities. Through doctrinal and comparative legal analysis, the project will explore the regulatory and administrative mechanisms for integrating DNSH throughout the public procurement lifecycle, considering developments in EU sustainable finance and public expenditure frameworks.
